name: Woodcut
summary: A print from a block of wood with the white parts cut away; the result is flat colour, hard edges and visible grain.
how: Cut the block along the grain with a knife and a gouge; leave a line of 1mm to 3mm for the black.
Use one block for each colour and register them within 1 mm.
Print with a flat, opaque ink and leave the grain and the knife marks visible.
Keep the shapes flat, with no more than 3 to 6 tones in a print.

origin.note: The Diamond Sutra, printed in China in 868, is the oldest dated printed book made from woodblocks.

adoptions.via: Michael Wolgemut and Wilhelm Pleydenwurff design the 1,809 woodcuts of the Nuremberg Chronicle, which Anton Koberger prints with the text.
Lucas Cranach the Elder and Hans Burgkmair print woodcuts from a line block and tone blocks; Ugo da Carpi follows in Italy.
Workshops in Dong Ho and Yangliuqing print an outline block and flat colour blocks for New Year pictures.
Hu Zhengyan's Ten Bamboo Studio in Nanjing publishes its Manual of Painting and Calligraphy. The studio fits many small pearwood blocks into one picture and presses dry blocks for raised lines.
Print shops in Moscow and Kyiv cut cheap picture sheets on wood, and hand colourists paint them for sale by pedlars.
Suzuki Harunobu and his printers make the full-colour nishiki-e print on many blocks.
Suzuki Harunobu and his printers make the full-colour nishiki-e print in Edo, with one block for each colour and a kento register.
Poetry clubs in Edo pay for surimono, small prints on thick paper with embossing and metal dust.
The oldest invitation to a senjafuda exchange meeting that survives is from 1799. The slips are printed from woodblocks.
Bengali craftsmen cut woodblock pictures for books and sheets printed in the Battala quarter of Calcutta.
Meiji printers use imported aniline dye on woodblocks, and Kobayashi Kiyochika adds light and shadow in his kosen-ga.
William Morris draws woodcut borders and initials for the Kelmscott Press, cut by William Harcourt Hooper and others.
Paul Gauguin cuts the woodcuts of the Noa Noa series with flat colour and rough cuts.
Cutters in the Brazilian northeast cut woodblock covers for cordel chapbooks, from about 1900.
Yamamoto Kanae cuts and prints his own block for the print Fisherman, and so starts the sosaku-hanga movement.
Ernst Ludwig Kirchner, Erich Heckel and Karl Schmidt-Rottluff of Die Brücke cut jagged woodcuts in Dresden.
Die Brücke artists cut rough woodcuts in Dresden, with flat shapes and visible gouge marks.
André Derain and Maurice de Vlaminck cut woodcuts with flat colour and rough gouge marks.
Watanabe Shozaburo restarts the three-trade woodblock shop in Tokyo and names its prints shin-hanga.
Lu Xun leads a woodcut class in Shanghai, and young artists cut black-and-white prints on cheap wood.
